title: Elodie and the Wolf
premise: Coral Ashgrove, a mercenary bound to a silent god and trapped in a valley where magic cannot follow, watches the border wards collapse on the night every star goes dark. Crossing into a world gone strange, they discover that Elodie, the child they raised as their own, was sold at birth to the court beneath the mountain, and her stolen soul is the final payment keeping that court's ancient bargain alive. Hunted by the god's other servants and bargained with by things wearing familiar faces, Coral must decide whether survival was ever worth what it cost. In the end Coral trades their own sworn soul for Elodie's, shattering the bargain, restoring the stars, and building a new kind of family from the wreckage.
about_author: Tamsin Reyes is a former archivist who writes fantasy about debts, oaths, and the people we choose. She lives in a drafty coastal town where she keeps an unreasonable number of maps of places that do not exist.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot Magic
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A quiet patrol along the valley's ward-stones establishes Coral's life: mercenary work, a mute god's mark on their wrist, and twelve-year-old Elodie waiting at home. The wards hum wrong tonight. Emotional beat: uneasy domesticity before the storm.

chapters.title: Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Every star vanishes at once, and the border wards fall like cut ropes. Magic floods the valley for the first time in generations, and something vast moves beneath the mountain. Coral grabs Elodie and runs. Emotional beat: terror and disorientation.

chapters.title: What Followed Us Home
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Hiding in the root cellar, Elodie hears the thing searching the house call her by a name she has never been told. She realizes it isn't hunting Coral at all. Emotional beat: the ground truth of her identity cracks open.

chapters.title: The Mark That Answers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral's god-mark burns awake for the first time in years, pulling them toward the mountain like a hook in flesh. An old comrade, Vess, arrives with news: the god didn't go silent — it was devoured. Emotional beat: betrayal of everything Coral believed.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Crossroads
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the fallen ward-line, a masked broker offers passage and protection in exchange for a promise Coral can't yet read. Desperate, they sign. Elodie watches them do it. Emotional beat: love used as leverage.

chapters.title: Road Through the Dark Country
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The trio travels a land where night never lifts, meeting refugees who traded memories to survive. Elodie begins hearing the mountain singing to her. Emotional beat: found family tightening under pressure.

chapters.title: The Inn of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Sheltering with other servants of dead gods, Vess learns Coral's signed promise makes them legally property of the court below. She must choose between warning them and using them. Emotional beat: loyalty versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: Songs in Her Sleep
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The mountain's song grows louder, showing Elodie fragments of her birth: her mother's face, a contract, a price paid in souls. She stops telling Coral what she sees. Emotional beat: isolation inside closeness.

chapters.title: The Godless Chapel
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Seeking answers, Coral breaks into a chapel where the god once spoke, finding records of the original bargain: one soul per generation, owed to the court beneath the mountain. Their own name is in the ledger too. Emotional beat: horror of inherited debt.

chapters.title: Hunted by the Faithful
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Other god-sworn mercenaries, believing Coral stole the valley's magic, ambush them on a frozen river. Coral wins brutally and hates themselves for it. Elodie sees the violence up close for the first time. Emotional beat: the price of survival made visible.

chapters.title: What Vess Knew All Along
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Confronted, Vess confesses she helped arrange Elodie's sale years ago to buy the valley its safety. Coral's rage nearly destroys their friendship. Emotional beat: betrayal from within the family.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Guided by the broker's mark, they reach a door carved with the god's face, now cracked and weeping black light. It opens only for those who owe. Coral walks through carrying Elodie's hand. Emotional beat: crossing the point of no return.

chapters.title: Court of Quiet Teeth
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Below, Elodie meets the court: beautiful, patient things who greet her as 'the thirteenth payment.' They are courteous, generous, and absolutely certain she belongs to them. Emotional beat: seductive dread.

chapters.title: Ledger of Souls
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In the court's archive, Coral finds the full contract — and learns the god itself was the first debtor, devoured when it defaulted. The court has been collecting ever since. Emotional beat: the scale of the trap revealed.

chapters.title: Thirteen Generations
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Shown the twelve souls taken before her, still dreaming in glass, Elodie speaks with the first of them — a girl who remembers the sun. Elodie promises to free them all or die trying. Emotional beat: courage kindled.

chapters.title: The Broker's True Face
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The masked broker reveals themselves as the remnant of the devoured god, surviving inside its own debt. It offers Coral a way out that requires abandoning Elodie forever. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened to a knife.

chapters.title: Running Out of Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The court begins the collection ritual early; the last stars' remnants gutter overhead. Vess arrives with the godsworn mercenaries, offering a suicidal diversion. Old wounds don't heal, but old debts can be spent. Emotional beat: reconciliation bought with blood.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Cornered before the throne, Coral understands the only currency the court respects: a willing soul, freely given, worth more than a sold child's. They offer theirs — the oath, the mark, everything. Emotional beat: sacrifice as answer to the book's central question.

chapters.title: Where the Bargain Breaks
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. As Coral's soul is drawn out, Elodie seizes the contract itself and speaks the first debtor's forgotten name, voiding the original terms. The court's foundation cracks; the glass souls wake. Emotional beat: the powerless unmaking the powerful.

chapters.title: Stars Returning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The court collapses inward, the broker-god dissolving with something like gratitude. The twelve freed souls rise past them toward a sky where, one by one, stars reignite. Coral lies cold on the floor. Emotional beat: awe after ruin.

chapters.title: What We Owe Each Other
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie refuses to let the trade stand, arguing before whatever remains of the court's law that a soul freely offered can be freely refused. Something ancient agrees. Coral wakes, hollowed but breathing, in the ruins. Emotional beat: grace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Home Is a Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They walk back into a valley learning magic gently, wards rebuilt not to exclude but to welcome. Coral plants the god's broken mark in the earth like a seed; Elodie calls the place home without flinching. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace.
